Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (a Next.js 16 + Prisma app called Kodely — an AI website builder).

BUILD: user management for the admin panel. Today `/admin` shows cost and margin across all builds but there is no way to look at a single customer — no user list, no per-user detail. When someone emails "my build failed and I was charged", there is no way to answer them.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT FILES UNDER `app/admin/users/`
Do NOT touch `app/admin/page.tsx` or `app/admin/layout.tsx` — those are owned by someone else and being edited right now. You may READ them (read layout.tsx especially — it holds the authorization gate). Create `app/admin/users/page.tsx` and `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` plus any components you need in that directory.

## What to build
1. **User list** (`app/admin/users/page.tsx`) — email, signup date, role, project count, current credit balance, lifetime credits spent, lifetime imputed cost, build count. Sortable or at minimum sensibly ordered (most recent signups first is a fine default). Searchable by email. Paginated — do NOT load every user.

2. **User detail** (`app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx`) — their projects (name, slug, published state), their build history with status/model/tokens/cost/credits/repairAttempts, and their full credit ledger as a running statement (delta, reason, balanceAfter, date). The ledger view is the thing that answers billing questions, so make it genuinely readable — a customer asking "why am I out of credits" should be answerable from this page in ten seconds.

3. **A per-user event journey** if it is cheap — `lib/events.ts` (READ ONLY, do not edit) has an `Event` model indexed by `[userId, createdAt]`. A simple reverse-chronological list of that user's events is very useful for debugging "what did this person actually do".

## Critical constraints — read carefully
- **Authorization**: `app/admin/layout.tsx` gates the whole `/admin` section on `role === "ADMIN"`, and it also wraps your routes. But do NOT rely on it alone — Next's own docs say a layout must not be the sole authorization boundary. `lib/auth.ts` exports `getAdminUser()` which returns the user or null. Call it at the top of EVERY page you create and `notFound()` if null. Read `app/admin/page.tsx` to see the exact idiom already in use and match it.
- **This page displays other people's private data** — prompts, emails, generated content. That is legitimate for an operator, but be conservative: truncate prompts in list views, do not dump full generated file contents, and do not add any way to act on a user's behalf (no impersonation, no login-as, no editing their projects). Read-only.
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/, app/api/**, app/admin/page.tsx, app/admin/layout.tsx, app/projects/**, app/dashboard/**, app/settings/**, app/legal/**, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- DO NOT add npm dependencies.
- DO NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **Query efficiency matters** — the user list must not be N+1. Use `groupBy`/`aggregate`/`_count` rather than a query per user in a loop. Note that credit balance is derived: `getBalance` in lib/credits.ts reads `balanceAfter` off the NEWEST ledger row for a user; work out how to get that for many users without one query each, and explain your approach.
- Match the existing admin styling exactly: `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, `tabular-nums` on figures, monochrome. Read `app/admin/page.tsx` for the table and stat-tile patterns and reuse them.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint <your files>`; your files must be clean. Pre-existing errors elsewhere (PromptHero.tsx, ThemeToggle.tsx and a few others) are NOT yours.
- You may query the local Postgres (DATABASE_URL in .env) to check your queries work and to see real data shapes. Do NOT modify or delete any data.

## Report back
What you built, how you avoided N+1 on the balance lookup, what you verified against the real database, and anything you found in the data that looks wrong.

Built and verified. Everything lives under `app/admin/users/`; nothing else in the tree was touched.

## What I built

**`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\admin\users\page.tsx`** — user list. Email (linked to detail), signup date, role, project count, build count with succeeded/failed split, current credit balance, lifetime credits spent, lifetime imputed cost. Search box matches email *or* name case-insensitively *or* an exact user id pasted from a log line. Sort by newest/oldest/email/project-count. Paginated at 25/page with prev-next links that preserve query and sort.

**`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\admin\users\[id]\page.tsx`** — user detail. Six stat tiles (balance, lifetime granted, lifetime spent + 30-day window, builds, imputed cost, margin), an amber "Needs a look" banner, the credit statement, projects, build history, and the event journey.

**`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\admin\users\ui.tsx`** — shared presentational helpers (`StatTile`, `Panel`, `TableFrame`, `Th`, `formatUsd`, `truncate`, `statusClass`, `reasonLabel`). Not a route; Next's generated `validator.ts` confirms only the two `page.tsx` files were registered as routes.

The ledger is the centrepiece: newest-first statement with date, decoded reason, the build it was charged against plus that build's status, signed delta in red/emerald, `balanceAfter`, and a thin balance-trajectory bar per row reusing the funnel-bar pattern from `/admin` — so "when did they run dry" is a glance rather than a column of numbers to diff. `reasonLabel` decodes the three encodings `reason` actually carries (`build`, `signup_grant`, `stripe:<session>`, and the `reward:<platform>:[pending:]<identityHash>` state machine from `app/api/rewards/_lib.ts`) so a 64-char hex blob never lands in the middle of a billing statement; the raw string stays on hover.

Authorization: `getAdminUser()` at the top of both pages with `notFound()`, matching the idiom and the comment in `app/admin/page.tsx`. Read-only throughout — no impersonation, no mutations, prompts truncated to 60 chars, errors to 70, no file contents anywhere.

## Avoiding N+1 on the balance lookup

`getBalance` reads `balanceAfter` off a user's newest ledger row. For a page of users that's one `findFirst` each. Instead I do it in a single pass with Postgres `DISTINCT ON`:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT ON (l."userId") l."userId", l."balanceAfter"
FROM "CreditLedger" l
WHERE l."userId" IN (…)
ORDER BY l."userId", l."createdAt" DESC, l."id" DESC
```

`id DESC` is the tiebreak so two rows written inside the same millisecond resolve to the same row Prisma's `findFirst` would pick. I verified this against `getBalance`'s exact Prisma path for every user — identical results.

`Build` has no `userId` (it hangs off `Project`), so the per-user build rollup is one grouped join with `FILTER (WHERE status = …)` for the succeeded/failed split rather than a count per user. Spend and net-delta come from two `groupBy` calls with `userId IN (…)`. Total: **6 queries for the list page regardless of page size** — count, users, balances, builds, spent, net. No query runs inside a loop.

One deliberate limitation: I only offer **database-native** sorts. Balance, spend and build count are derived per-page, so offering them as sort options would silently sort 25 arbitrary rows instead of the table — worse than not offering it. That is commented in the file.

Free bonus from the same query set: the ledger is append-only and starts at zero, so `sum(delta)` must equal the newest `balanceAfter`. Comparing them costs one extra grouped query and surfaces a drifted ledger before a customer does — shown as a "Ledger drift" tile and a per-row `!`. The detail page does the same check row-by-row from data already in hand.

## Verified against the real database

Ran every query from both pages against `kodely_personal` (read-only). All four sort orders, five search cases including the id-paste path and a no-match, both raw queries (column aliases and `::int`/`::bigint` casts come back with the exact keys and types the code expects), all twelve detail-page queries per user, and the missing-user `notFound` path. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` are clean on all three files (pre-existing errors in `HeroMock.tsx`/`__assets.mts` are not mine — note `HeroMock.tsx` errors appeared *during* my session, so someone is mid-edit there). Both routes compile on the running dev server and correctly 307 to `/dashboard` for an unauthenticated request.

One lint finding worth knowing: `react-hooks/purity` rejects `Date.now()` in a server component render. I removed my inline 30-day window and now call `spentInWindow()` from `lib/credits.ts` instead — which is better anyway, since the number shown is now literally the one the spend cap enforces.

I could not visually render the pages: doing so needs an ADMIN session, and creating one would mean writing to the database.

## What looks wrong in the data

1. **No user has `role === "ADMIN"`.** All three are `CUSTOMER`. The entire `/admin` section — the existing dashboard included — is currently unreachable by every account in this database.
2. **A build was charged 1 credit for zero metered cost.** Build `cmt3536220001u7j4p3f3ycsh`, model `claude-agent-sdk-subscription`: 0 input, 0 output, 0 cache, `costMicros: 0`, `creditsCharged: 1`, with a matching `-1` ledger row. `creditsFor()` floors at `Math.max(1, …)`, so any zero-cost build still bills a credit. Tiny in money, but it is a charge for spend that provably did not happen, in the one module whose stated purpose is never doing that — and the subscription code path produces zero-cost builds by design, so this is systematic rather than a one-off.
3. **8 of 10 builds failed**, almost all on auth (`Not logged in · Please run /login`, `401 OAuth`), plus one Windows `EPERM … symlink` and one `EBUSY … rmdir`. Local-environment noise, but it means the green-build-rate numbers on `/admin` are computed off two successes.
4. **Failed builds record `model: ""`.** The model is only written on success, so the Model column is blank for every failure — I render an em-dash rather than an empty cell. Worth fixing at the write site: a failed build with no model recorded can't be attributed to a model regression.
5. **A FAILED build reports `filesWritten: 9`** (`cmt347k500001u7w47udrgl9y` — wrote files, then died on the symlink). So `filesWritten` is not a safe "did anything happen" signal on failures.
6. **The `Event` table is completely empty (0 rows).** The journey panel renders an explanatory empty state, but it is worth confirming `track()` is actually wired into the live signup/build/publish paths — the activation funnel on `/admin` is reading from the same empty table.
7. Ledger integrity itself is currently perfect: for all three users the newest `balanceAfter` equals the sum of all deltas, and no charge points at a non-succeeded build.
